title: Design frontmatter
description: Frontmatter for a design document under a specification directory. A design is a child of the specification it sits under: it carries `spec` naming its parent and has no `id` and no `status` of its own, because its lifecycle is its parent's. A design whose parent is accepted is accepted.

type.description: Document category, from the standard's closed set.

spec.description: The parent specification's identifier. A child's identity is this plus its filename, written SPEC-0004/design where a cross-reference needs one.

updated.description: Optional. Git already knows when the file changed; set this only where the document's own sense of currency differs from its last commit.

reviewed.description: Date a person or agent deliberately checked the document against reality and found it still true. Set it only where a review cadence has been declared.

owners.description: Who is answerable for the content. The first entry is the one answerable.

related.description: Declared relationships. Optional, so an absent relation proves nothing.

depends_on.description: Documents this one depends on. A separate field from `related`, not a relation within it.

url.description: Canonical location, for a document that gets copied out of the repository.

discussion.description: Where the argument happened: the pull request, issue or thread. Carried on the types that are argued before they are settled.

identifier.description: A document identifier such as SPEC-0012, ADR-0017 or ARCH-SECURITY.

target.description: A reference resolvable from outside this document: an identifier (SPEC-0004), a qualified identifier (lexicon:SPEC-0004), an issue or pull request (argus#142), or a repository-relative path to a document that has no identifier (docs/plans/2026-09-11-project-doc-template.md). A path target is never qualified with a repository prefix.

relatedEntry.description: One declared relationship, as a predicate and what it points at.

$comment: A child of a specification, per the standard's metadata.md: "`design`, `research` and `verification` are children of a specification. A child document carries `spec:` holding its parent's identifier, for instance `spec: SPEC-0004`, and no `id` and no `status` of its own." The three child schemas are identical apart from the `type` const; nothing distinguishes them at the frontmatter level, and inventing a difference to justify three files would be worse than the repetition. They are three because `type` is a closed set and a validator resolves a schema by the type it finds. `supersedes` and `superseded_by` are absent rather than optional: both name an identifier, and a child has none. A child is referenced as SPEC-0004/design, which the standard names, and superseding one is a change to its parent.
